item.title: SNB Rate Forecasts Now Anctipate Hike in Mid-2027 at Earliest
item.description: Swiss National Bank forecasters pushed back predictions for an interest-rate increase, with no move anticipated before next June at the earliest.

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks, Currencies Gain After Soft US Jobs Data
item.description: Emerging-market stocks and currencies climbed at the start of a new week as expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes eased following Friday’s unexpectedly weak US employment report.

item.title: Euro Zone Set for Firmer Growth After Bumper Second Quarter
item.description: Economic growth in the euro zone is set to quicken after showing surprising resilience to the Iran war, according to a Bloomberg survey of analysts.

item.title: Romania Set to Keep Rates at 6.5%, EU’s Highest, on Political Turmoil
item.description: Romania is likely to hold borrowing costs unchanged at the highest level in the European Union as a lengthy political crisis clouds the economic and inflation outlook.

item.title: Indonesian Stocks Near Bull Market as Economic Worries Recede
item.description: Indonesian stocks advanced, putting the benchmark index once again near bull-market territory, as investor sentiment was buoyed by signs of a resilient economy and easing concerns over potential market downgrades.

item.title: Rotation From Leveraged ETFs Fuel 30% Jump in Korea Small Caps
item.description: South Korea’s small-cap stocks are regaining investor interest after lagging larger peers for much of the year, as restrictions on leveraged exchanged-traded funds tracking heavyweight chipmakers shift money toward Kosdaq names.

item.title: Yen Underperforms G-10 Peers as Intervention Boost Fades
item.description: The yen has underperformed all its Group-of-10 peers this month as the boost from recent intervention fades, putting traders on alert for further official action.

item.title: Wheat Hits Highest in a Week on Supply Disruptions in Black Sea
item.description: US wheat futures jumped to the highest in more than a week, as disruptions to shipping in the Black Sea raised the prospect of supply shortages from the crucial grain-growing region.

item.title: Sony, TSMC to Invest $6.4 Billion in Japanese Sensor Plant
item.description: Sony Group Corp. and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. are in talks to spend a combined ¥1 trillion ($6.4 billion) on their planned image sensor factory in Japan, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: India’s FX Reserves Climb Toward Record on Foreign Inflows
item.description: Stockpile rises for five straight weeks, the longest run since April 2025.

item.title: Shein Valued at $22 Billion to $25 Billion Ahead of IPO, BI Says
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd.’s fast-fashion niche supports a valuation of $22 billion to $25 billion, Bloomberg Intelligence said, putting a fresh marker on one of the biggest questions surrounding the retailer as it prepares for one of the year’s biggest initial public offerings.

item.title: Australia Widens Orders on Chinese Investors in Rare Earths Firm
item.description: Australia has stepped in again to try to force some Chinese investors out of a rare earths mining firm, telling two parties that they will also need government approval before selling their holdings to ensure the shares aren’t sold to any related parties.

item.title: Australian Scandium Miner Soars After $400 Million US Investment
item.description: Sunrise Energy Metals Ltd. shares soared after the Australian scandium miner secured as much as $400 million in long-term debt financing from the US Department of War.

item.title: HFTs Shun India Stock Closing Auction Over SEBI Short-Selling Hurdle
item.description: India’s new method of setting official closing prices for its stocks is drawing complaints from some of the firms that do the most to keep its $5.2 trillion market humming along.

item.title: India’s UPI Payments Developer Targets Diaspora For Growth
item.description: The operator of India’s ubiquitous mobile payments network plans to tap the country’s vast overseas diaspora as a springboard for global expansion, aiming to make the platform a preferred way to transact money across borders.

item.title: BOJ Flags Upside Price Risks and Possible Faster Rate Hikes
item.description: The Bank of Japan flagged rising risks of inflation heating up in a summary of opinions from its July meeting, with one board member pointing to the possibility of an acceleration in the pace of interest rate hikes.

item.title: DatVietVAC Advances Vietnam IPO as It Looks to Korea Playbook
item.description: DatVietVAC Group Holdings., producer of some of Vietnam’s highest-rated television programs, is pursuing an initial public offering as it seeks to replicate the success of South Korea’s entertainment giants.

item.title: Gold Holds Gain After Soft US Jobs Data Eases Rate-Hike Concerns
item.description: Gold steadied after its biggest weekly gain since January, with traders assessing a surprise contraction in the US jobs market that allayed concerns around an interest-rate hike.

item.title: Jetstar, Qatar Air Near Miss at Sydney Triggers Safety Probe
item.description: An air safety investigation is underway after a Jetstar plane and a Qatar Airways jet almost collided on the tarmac at Sydney airport on Sunday — the second near miss in two weeks.

item.title: Treasury Wine Shares Soar After Moves to Tackle Excess US Supply
item.description: Australian vintner Treasury Wine Estates Ltd. saw its shares jump to an eight-month high after announcing a A$558.4 million ($395 million) post-tax writedown to tackle supply chain problems in its US market.

item.title: UK Hiring Turns a Corner After Longest Slump on Record, REC Says
item.description: Hiring at British businesses held steady in July, ending a downturn stretching back to the Liz Truss crisis in 2022, according to a closely watched survey.

item.title: How David Ellison Won Over Major Movie Theaters
item.description: The world’s two largest movie theater chains just backed a merger that their peers oppose

item.title: Oil Gains as Iran Deal Eludes, Stocks Set to Rise: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil extended its gains in early Monday trading as Iran rejected talks with the US and a deal to reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz remained elusive. Asian stocks looked set to advance in catch-up trading.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 10
item.description: Oil extended gains as Iran and Oman remained short of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Houthi militants claimed an attack on a Saudi refinery near the Red Sea.

item.title: Westpac CEO Flags Moderating Housing Market, Profit Edges Up
item.description: Westpac Banking Corp.’s profit expanded slightly as deposit and loan growth offset caution on the housing market from the lender’s chief executive.

item.title: China Bets on AI Stocks as It Races Against US for Chip, Tech Dominance
item.description: The strategy marks a break from Beijing’s reliance on subsidies and state funding.

item.title: Aussie-Yen Is Set to Approach Three-Decade High, Analysts Say
item.description: The Australian dollar is poised to climb back toward a 35-year high against the yen as the impact of Tokyo’s currency intervention fades and the Reserve Bank of Australia’s hawkish stance bolsters the exchange rate, according to strategists.

item.title: RBA Set for Hawkish Hold and Alert to Persistent Price Pressures
item.description: Australia’s central bank is poised to keep interest rates unchanged for a second straight meeting on Tuesday, while restating its readiness to tighten policy further in order to tackle stubbornly strong inflation.

item.title: Australian Wheat Crop Rebounds at Crucial Time for Global Supply
item.description: Prospects for Australia’s upcoming wheat crop are turning more optimistic, helping to buffer an increasingly grim global supply outlook for the grain.

item.title: Hungarian Central Banker Touts Benefits of Joining Euro Area
item.description: Hungary’s central bank renewed its support for the government’s efforts to meet conditions for joining the euro area, saying it would benefit the economy.
